evals.name: node-postgres-staging
evals.prompt: Deploy this Next.js app to my Dokploy install, staging env. The repo is at /tmp/yalla-fixtures/node-postgres. My Dokploy is at https://ploy.jsa.sa, base host for autodomains is apps.jsa.sa. Don't actually run anything destructive — just give me the full plan with every yalla call I'd need to run, in order, including the JSON bodies. The repo has a Prisma schema using postgres and a .env.example with several vars I want shipped.
evals.expected: nixpacks build, postgres provisioned, full env-var partition, both envs created, letsencrypt domain

evals.name: static-spa-prod
evals.prompt: Push this Vite-built site to Dokploy production. Path: /tmp/yalla-fixtures/static-spa. No database, no env vars. Use Let's Encrypt. Just walk me through the steps and yalla calls.
evals.expected: static build, isStaticSpa=true, no DB ops, deploy in production env

evals.name: compose-stack
evals.prompt: I have a docker-compose stack at /tmp/yalla-fixtures/compose-stack with an api service, a worker, and a postgres. Deploy it to my Dokploy as a compose stack in staging. Skip the domain auto-creation if it makes things complicated.
evals.expected: compose-create with composeFile inline, no application-create, no postgres-create, compose-deploy

evals.name: dockerfile-multistage-go
evals.prompt: Deploy this Go service to staging on my Dokploy at ploy.jsa.sa, base host apps.jsa.sa. The repo at /tmp/yalla-fixtures/dockerfile-multistage-go has a multi-stage Dockerfile (build stage + alpine runtime, EXPOSE 8080) and a .env.example mentioning DATABASE_URL=postgres://. Paper plan only — show every yalla call with full JSON bodies.
evals.expected: buildType=dockerfile, dockerfile=./Dockerfile, dockerContextPath=., postgres-create, domain port=8080, git-provider with origin URL

evals.name: python-heroku-buildpacks
evals.prompt: I have a Flask app at /tmp/yalla-fixtures/python-heroku-buildpacks with a Procfile (web + worker), requirements.txt (Flask + gunicorn + psycopg2-binary + redis), and a .env.example mentioning DATABASE_URL=postgres:// and REDIS_URL=redis://. Deploy to staging on my Dokploy at ploy.jsa.sa, base host apps.jsa.sa. Paper plan only.
evals.expected: buildType=heroku_buildpacks, herokuVersion populated, postgres-create AND redis-create, env vars wired

evals.name: railpack-app
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/railpack-app to my Dokploy production at ploy.jsa.sa, base host apps.jsa.sa. It has a railpack.json (Bun + Hono). No DB. Paper plan with every yalla call.
evals.expected: buildType=railpack, railpackVersion populated, no DB ops, deploy to production

evals.name: docker-image-only
evals.prompt: I want to deploy the docker image ghcr.io/example/api:v1.4.0 to my Dokploy at ploy.jsa.sa (base host apps.jsa.sa) staging env. Listening on port 3000. There's no source code locally — just the image (the directory at /tmp/yalla-fixtures/docker-image-only has only a DEPLOY.md noting the image ref and port). Paper plan with all yalla calls.
evals.expected: application-saveDockerProvider with dockerImage=ghcr.io/example/api:v1.4.0, no git-provider call, domain port=3000, deploy

evals.name: monorepo-subpath
evals.prompt: In /tmp/yalla-fixtures/monorepo-subpath I have a monorepo with /apps/web (Next.js) and /apps/api (Express + pg). Deploy ONLY the api (/apps/api) to my Dokploy staging at ploy.jsa.sa, base host apps.jsa.sa. Paper plan only.
evals.expected: customGitBuildPath=/apps/api, nixpacks build, postgres-create, env vars from /apps/api/.env.example

evals.name: multi-db
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/multi-db to my Dokploy staging at ploy.jsa.sa, base host apps.jsa.sa. It's a Node app with pg + ioredis + mongoose dependencies and a .env.example referencing DATABASE_URL (postgres), REDIS_URL, and MONGO_URL. Paper plan with full yalla calls.
evals.expected: postgres-create AND redis-create AND mongo-create, all 3 deploy ops, application-saveEnvironment with all 3 connection strings injected

evals.name: redeploy-existing
evals.prompt: Redeploy the project at /tmp/yalla-fixtures/redeploy-existing to its staging env. It has a .dokploy.yaml from a previous deploy with project + env + app IDs already saved. Paper plan only — the skill should recognise this and skip creation steps.
evals.expected: skill detects .dokploy.yaml, calls application-redeploy with the saved applicationId, does NOT call project-create / environment-create / application-create

evals.name: ambiguous-multi-builder
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/ambiguous-multi-builder to my Dokploy staging at ploy.jsa.sa, base host apps.jsa.sa. The repo has Dockerfile + Procfile + railpack.json + package.json (all four). Pick the right build type and tell me why. Paper plan.
evals.expected: skill notices the ambiguity, picks dockerfile per priority order, calls out the alternatives explicitly so the user can override

evals.name: preflight-not-ready
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/preflight-not-ready to my Dokploy at ploy.jsa.sa. ASSUME yalla is not yet installed/authenticated on this machine — `yalla --version` would say 'command not found' or `yalla auth status` would say `ready: false`. Walk me through what to do.
evals.expected: skill stops at preflight, emits setup instructions (build, yalla auth login with --url, token-stdin automation alternative, auth status/whoami verification), does not produce a deploy plan

evals.name: tear-down-existing
evals.prompt: Tear down the deployment at /tmp/yalla-fixtures/tear-down-existing. Remove everything from Dokploy — project, apps, envs, domains. There's a .dokploy.yaml with the IDs. Paper plan.
evals.expected: skill reads .dokploy.yaml, plan calls project-remove with the saved projectId (cascades), does NOT call project-create / application-create / etc.

evals.name: background-worker-no-domain
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/background-worker — a queue worker (BullMQ + ioredis), no HTTP endpoint. Dokploy at ploy.jsa.sa, staging env. Skip domain (no public access needed). Paper plan.
evals.expected: redis-create (REDIS_URL detected), nixpacks build, no domain-create call, application-deploy + status-poll only (no HTTP probe in verification)

evals.name: custom-domain
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/custom-domain to my Dokploy at ploy.jsa.sa. I want to use my own domain `api.acme.com` for production — NOT the auto-named `<project>-<env>.<base-host>` default. DNS for api.acme.com already points at the Dokploy server. Use Let's Encrypt. Paper plan with full yalla calls.
evals.expected: domain-create body uses host='api.acme.com' (NOT auto-named), targets production env, certificateType=letsencrypt, https=true

evals.name: multi-domain
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/multi-domain to my Dokploy production at ploy.jsa.sa. ONE app, but I need TWO public hosts: `api.acme.com` and `admin.acme.com`. Both Let's Encrypt, same applicationId. Paper plan.
evals.expected: TWO separate domain-create calls — same applicationId, different hosts, both letsencrypt

evals.name: custom-path-routing
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/path-routed-api to my Dokploy production. The app should respond at `acme.com/api/*` (path-prefix routing — there are other apps living at the same domain). The internal app expects requests at root `/`, so strip the `/api` prefix before forwarding. Paper plan with the domain-create body — show `path`, `internalPath`, and `stripPath` correctly set.
evals.expected: domain-create body has host=acme.com, path=/api, stripPath=true (or internalPath=/), explicitly explains the stripPath behaviour

evals.name: custom-cert
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/custom-cert to my Dokploy production. We have our own corporate TLS cert + custom Traefik resolver named `corp-vault-resolver` (already configured Dokploy-side). Domain `internal.acme.corp`. Don't use Let's Encrypt — use our custom cert. Paper plan.
evals.expected: domain-create body has certificateType=custom, customCertResolver='corp-vault-resolver', https=true

evals.name: private-git-ssh
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/private-git-ssh to my Dokploy staging. The repo is private at `git@github.com:acme/private-svc.git`. I have an SSH key already registered in Dokploy with id `SSH-KEY-DOKPLOY-9876`. Has a Dockerfile. Paper plan.
evals.expected: application-saveGitProvider body uses customGitUrl='git@github.com:acme/private-svc.git', customGitSSHKeyId='SSH-KEY-DOKPLOY-9876', dockerfile build type

evals.name: private-registry-image
evals.prompt: Deploy the private docker image at `registry.acme.com/billing/api:v3.2.1` to my Dokploy staging. Username `billing-deploy`, password is in 1Password — I'll paste it when prompted. Listens on port 8080. The directory at /tmp/yalla-fixtures/private-registry only has a DEPLOY.md noting this. Paper plan.
evals.expected: application-saveDockerProvider body has dockerImage=registry.acme.com/billing/api:v3.2.1, registryUrl=https://registry.acme.com, username='billing-deploy', explicit note that password should be supplied via prompt/credential store/env var (NOT pasted in chat), domain port=8080

evals.name: github-app-provider
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/github-app-provider to my Dokploy staging. We have a Dokploy↔GitHub App configured — its ID is in `.dokploy.yaml` under `github_provider_id`. Use `application-saveGithubProvider` with that ID so push-to-main triggers redeploys automatically. Paper plan.
evals.expected: application-saveGithubProvider body uses githubId from the .dokploy.yaml, owner='acme', repository='shop', triggerType='push', branch='main'

evals.name: promote-staging-to-prod
evals.prompt: Promote the staging deployment at /tmp/yalla-fixtures/promote-staging to production. Staging is already live (.dokploy.yaml has the staging app + env). The production env exists but has NO application yet. Reuse the same git source/build type as staging but with the DIFFERENT env vars from `.env.production` (DATABASE_URL points at prod-db, NODE_ENV=production, SENTRY_ENV=production). Don't recreate the project or staging env. Paper plan.
evals.expected: skill recognises .dokploy.yaml, reuses project + production env, creates a NEW application in the production env, copies source/build config from staging, applies .env.production vars, calls application-deploy on the new prod app — does NOT touch the staging app

evals.name: external-managed-database
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/external-managed-db to my Dokploy staging. The .env.example has DATABASE_URL pointing at our managed Postgres on AWS RDS (`prod-db.cluster-xyz.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com`). DO NOT provision a Dokploy postgres — the app should connect to RDS directly. Paper plan.
evals.expected: skill detects DATABASE_URL but recognises the external host (RDS / non-local FQDN) and SKIPS postgres-create / postgres-deploy. application-saveEnvironment ships the DATABASE_URL verbatim. Domain still set up. Plan calls out the assumption explicitly.

evals.name: app-with-migrations
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/django-with-migrations to my Dokploy staging at ploy.jsa.sa. Django app, has a `release: python manage.py migrate --noinput` line in the Procfile — that's the schema migration that MUST run before any web traffic. Paper plan should make sure migrations run before/at-deploy, not skipped.
evals.expected: skill recognises the Procfile `release:` line and configures heroku_buildpacks build (which honours release commands), OR explicitly notes that yalla/Dokploy may need a custom pre-deploy command via application-update (or similar). Plan must NOT silently drop the migrate step.

evals.name: rollback-previous-deploy
evals.prompt: The last production deploy at /tmp/yalla-fixtures/rollback-needed shipped a broken release (`ghcr.io/acme/api:v2.4.1`). Roll back to the known-good `ghcr.io/acme/api:v2.4.0`. The .dokploy.yaml records both image tags. Paper plan with the yalla calls.
evals.expected: plan calls application-saveDockerProvider with dockerImage='ghcr.io/acme/api:v2.4.0' (the previous-good tag) on the existing applicationId, then application-redeploy. Does NOT call project-create / application-create. Mentions checking the rollback succeeded via application-one + HTTP probe.

evals.name: stop-without-tear-down
evals.prompt: Stop (don't delete) the production deployment at /tmp/yalla-fixtures/stop-app. Keep all the config — domain, env vars, database — intact, just stop the running container so we can investigate something. Paper plan.
evals.expected: plan calls application-stop with the saved applicationId. Does NOT call project-remove / application-delete / domain-* / postgres-*. Mentions application-start as the inverse op for resuming later.

evals.name: cron-scheduled
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/cron-scheduled to my Dokploy production at ploy.jsa.sa, base host apps.jsa.sa. SCHEDULE.md says it should run nightly at 02:30 UTC via cron `30 2 * * *`. NOT a long-running web service — a periodic batch job. Paper plan.
evals.expected: plan uses Dokploy's schedule mechanism (schedule-create or similar) with the cron expression, NOT application-create + domain-create. Does NOT attach a domain. Skips domain HTTP probe in verification.

evals.name: scaling-replicas
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/scaling-replicas to my Dokploy production. SCALE.md says 3 replicas, 512Mi memory, 0.5 CPU each. Paper plan with the yalla call that sets replicas + resource limits.
evals.expected: plan calls application-update (or saveResources / similar) with replicas=3, memory limit, CPU limit. Standard app-create flow + the resource configuration step. Domain on port 3000 with letsencrypt.

evals.name: multi-server-placement
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/multi-server-placement to my Dokploy. The cluster has multiple servers — PLACEMENT.md says this app MUST run on the GPU node (serverId: SERVER-GPU-01). Paper plan that pins the app to that server.
evals.expected: plan sets serverId=SERVER-GPU-01 in application-create body. Does not leave serverId=null. Mentions that without this, the swarm scheduler could place the workload on a non-GPU node.

evals.name: volumes-persistent
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/volumes-persistent to my Dokploy production. The container writes to /data — VOLUMES.md says we need a NAMED volume `app-data` of 20Gi mounted at /data so redeploys preserve state. Paper plan with the volume/mount yalla call.
evals.expected: plan calls mount-create (or volume-create — yalla's mount op) with mountType=volume, mountName=app-data, mountPath=/data, applicationId. Volume call comes BEFORE application-deploy so first deploy sees the mount.

evals.name: deploy-notifications
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/deploy-notifications to my Dokploy production. NOTIFY.md says I want a Slack webhook fired on every deploy (success and failure). The webhook URL is in NOTIFY.md. Paper plan that wires notifications too.
evals.expected: plan calls notification-create with type=slack, webhook URL from NOTIFY.md, channel=#deploys. Then attaches the notification to the project/app via notification-* ops. Standard deploy lifecycle around it.

evals.name: websocket-app
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/websocket-app to my Dokploy production. It's a Socket.IO server — needs HTTP/1.1 upgrade for WebSocket and long idle timeouts (default 60s isn't enough). Domain ws.acme.com. Paper plan.
evals.expected: plan uses application-saveBuildType=nixpacks (Node app). Domain has https=true, letsencrypt, port 3000. Plan calls out the WebSocket needs explicitly: long Traefik timeouts (e.g. via application-update labels / domain settings), HTTP/1.1 upgrade, sticky sessions if replicas>1. Even if Dokploy handles WS natively, the plan must acknowledge the consideration.

evals.name: preview-deployments
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/preview-deployments to my Dokploy. PREVIEW.md says each PR to main should auto-deploy to <project>-pr-<num>.preview.acme.com as an ephemeral preview env. Paper plan.
evals.expected: plan calls Dokploy's previewDeployment-* ops (the spec has them) to set up per-PR ephemeral envs. Configures domain template using ${PR_NUMBER} or similar. Mentions that the GitHub provider must be wired (push trigger) for the auto-creation to work.

evals.name: inter-app-comms
evals.prompt: Deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/inter-app-comms to my Dokploy production. Two apps in ONE project: frontend (apps/frontend, Express) and backend (apps/backend, Express + pg). The frontend's BACKEND_URL env var must point at the backend's in-cluster hostname so they talk over Dokploy's swarm network. Paper plan.
evals.expected: plan creates ONE project, TWO applications (each with its own customGitBuildPath: /apps/frontend and /apps/backend). After backend is created, plan recovers its appName via application-one and wires `BACKEND_URL=http://<backend-appName>:4000` into the frontend's application-saveEnvironment. Postgres provisioned for backend. Both apps get domains, but frontend's BACKEND_URL is the LOAD-BEARING piece.

evals.prompt: I just got a release zip from our CI artifact archive (downloaded to /tmp/yalla-fixtures/drop-deploy/release-v0.4.2.zip — it's a built SPA, the root of the zip is the build output, index.html is at top-level). The app already exists on my Dokploy at https://ploy.jsa.sa called "marketing-site" (project "marketing", env "production"). Drop it. No domain change needed. Paper plan with every yalla call and the exact --input JSON, then walk me through the actual upload step.
evals.expected_output: Plan should route through drop-deploy (not git/redeploy). Should look up applicationId via application-all under the marketing project, call application-saveBuildType with static (because SPA + root build output), then call application-dropDeployment with files.zip pointing at the local path and dropBuildPath omitted or empty. Should mention dry-run first. Should NOT propose application-saveGitProvider or application-saveDockerProvider.

evals.prompt: deploy /tmp/yalla-fixtures/drop-deploy/lambda-bundle to dokploy. it's a python lambda i built and zipped — there's no git remote on this folder, no Dockerfile, and i don't want to push the build artifact to any registry. just want it running on my dokploy box. base host apps.jsa.sa. staging env. project name should default to the folder name. tell me everything you'll do and then do it (assume the zip already exists at /tmp/yalla-fixtures/drop-deploy/lambda-bundle/release.zip).
evals.expected_output: Should detect this as a drop-deploy case based on: pre-built zip + no git remote + no Dockerfile + user explicitly doesn't want a registry. Full fresh-deploy lifecycle (project-create → environment-create → application-create → application-saveBuildType → application-saveEnvironment → optionally domain-create → application-dropDeployment) with the multipart input shape. Should call out that there's no server-side rollback for drop deploys.

evals.prompt: upload my new build to the api-gateway app. the zip is at /tmp/yalla-fixtures/drop-deploy/api-gateway-v3.zip — but the actual build output is inside the zip at build/output/ (the rest is source for debugging). app is on https://ploy.jsa.sa, project "platform", env "production". dry-run first so i can paste the envelope into the change log, then ship it. last zip is at ./api-gateway-v2.zip in case we need to roll back.
evals.expected_output: Plan must set dropBuildPath to "build/output" (not omit it, not use root). Must dry-run first; the dry-run envelope is meant to be pasted, so the deterministic boundary + redacted file sentinel matter. Should acknowledge there's no server-side rollback and the user's own ./api-gateway-v2.zip is the rollback path — re-running application-dropDeployment against it.
